TESTIMONY OF JASON COONEY
IN SUPPORT
OF LD 2128
AN ACT TO REORGANIZE THE EMERGENCY MEDICAL SERVICES' BOARD TO IMPLEMENT THE RECOMMENDATIONS OF THE BLUE RIBBON COMMISSION TO STUDY EMERGENCY MEDICAL
SERVICES IN THE STATE
Senator Bailey, Representative Mathison, and esteemed members of the Committee On Health Coverage, Insurance and Financial Services
My name is Jason Cooney. I am a resident of the Town of Topsham and a licensed Paramedic in the State of Maine. I have been practicing and licensed in the State since I was in high school, over fifteen years ago. I currently work as a Licensing Agent within the Maine Office of Emergency Medical Services. I prepared this testimony on my own time and without using any State resources. This testimony is my personal testimony; it is not representative of the position or opinion of the Executive Branch of Government, the Department of Public Safety, or the Office of Maine Emergency Medical Services.
I am testifying in support of LD 2128, and to add critical information for the committee to consider in its deliberations.
Background
In 2004, an assessment of the Maine EMS System was performed by the EMSSTAR Group LLC of Annapolis, Maryland, under contract with the State of Maine, Department of Public Safety. This assessment identified on its 3rd page, the top three priorities of the system to include "The regulatory and system support functions must be separated, with the state EMS office executing the regulatory aspects of its legislative mandate". Subsequently to this report, in 2022, the Maine Emergency Medical Services' Board ("Board") and the legislature undertook work in parallel: The Board undertook development of a strategic plan for the system visioned upon where the Board wanted to be in 2035; the Legislature convened the first Blue Ribbon Commission to Study Emergency Medical Services in the State of Maine. Both of these processes engaged significant input by all of the stakeholders within our system. In 2023, the legislature convened a second Blue Ribbon commission to Study Emergency Medical Services in the State of Maine. The Board's strategic plan was released in 2023 as the "Plan for a Sustainable EMS System in the State of Maine" (hereafter "Vision 2035 Plan"), and addresses where the Board visioned the "Structure Within Government" of our system with a milestone of "The EMS Board is small and agile with nine members representing EMS regions and key stakeholder groups. It provides guidance on EMS system planning and development, provides

representative input from various Ems stakeholders and provides a check and balance in rulemaking". The Vision 2035 Plan was adopted by the Board with a unanimous vote on April 5, 2023 (see enclosed minutes). Separately, the legislature's report of the Blue Ribbon Commission to Study Emergency Medical Services in the State, released in January of 2024, included the recommendation, B-3, "The Legislature should support the proposed reorganization of the EMS Board, which would established a 9-member EMS Board charged with the strategic direction and oversight of the EMS system..." In the 132 legislature's first special session, P.L. 2025 Ch. 520, required as emergency legislation that "By December 3, 2025, the Department of Public Safety, Maine Emergency Medical Services shall submit...a report, including proposed draft legislation, for the reorganization of the Emergency Medical Services' Board...consistent with the document titled "Maine EMS: Two-Year Action Plan"..." while this legislation was not approved until after the statutory deadline, the Department of Public Safety submitted proposed draft legislation for this body to consider.
The current Board is comprised of sixteen (16) members, 6 of which are currently vacant. Additionally, this Board has overlap in representation; 32 M.R.S. � 88(1)(A), establishes the composition of this Board to have "...one member representing each region and 12 person in addition. Of the additional persons...one a fire chief, one a representative of a statewide association of fire chiefs, one a municipal emergency medical services provider..." Of the currently ten appointed members, the Board has: Two (2) regional representatives that serve with a fire department, one as a Deputy Chief of the Westbrook Fire Department and one as the Deputy Chief of the Presque Isle Fire Department; A municipal representative that is currently employed by the Falmouth Fire Department; a member who is a Fire Chief; and a member representative of the Maine Fire Chiefs Association.
Discussion
The focus of the testimony is twofold: supportive of the reorganization of the Board to a slimmer, more agile 9-member composition, and supportive of the re-structing of the membership of the Board. The support of the reorganization of the Board to a smaller group, I hope, is firmly established by the above background; the Board, the Legislature, and an independent assessment all recommend that a smaller Board is in the system's best long-term interests. The restructuring of the membership of this Board, is where this discussion is best kept.
As outlined above, currently, five (5) of the currently ten (10) appointed and serving members of the Board are employed by, or represent, the interests of fire-based Emergency Medical Services. While fire-based Emergency Medical Services make up more than half of all emergency medical services in the State of Maine, the intent of the diverse representation of this Board is to garner opinions from a wide variety of stakeholders as opposed to a narrow

focus on the interests of one subset of the current industry. The legislation, as proposed, maintains the regional representation, and adds five (5) additional persons appointed by the Governor, selected by the function that they serve within our system, rather than the special interest group within our industry the current model provides. It also makes a major shift within our system by providing that instead of a nomination process leading to a regional representative selected by the Governor, the regional councils directly appoint a member to the Board. When it comes to policy making, Maine EMS has frequently been criticized as not representative of the wishes of its stakeholders - this change seems directly responsive and supportive of a local voice reaching the Board. It makes that regional representative responsible to the regional council, whose composition is designed to represent the local services provided in that area - as fire-based EMS holds the majority of services, that proportionality of interest can be best covered by this regional role, without dominating the totality of the voice on the Board. Another key addition to this Board is the representative of municipal administration. Maine EMS's policies often directly impact a municipality's budget through the promulgation of rules that impact a services license owned or contracted with that municipality. As such, it is key to ensure that this body, charged with the planning and system rulemaking, has a clear voice for the city and town administrators in the State of Maine who can lend their expertise, as well as serve as a conduit for greater understanding of EMS in Maine by those who lead our municipalities.
I strongly urge the members of this committee to support LD 2128 as currently drafted.

Testimony of the Maine Ambulance Association Before the Maine Health Coverage and Financial Services Committee in Support of
LD 2128
An Act to Reorganize the Emergency Medical Services Board to implement the Recommendations of the Blue Ribbon Commission to Study Emergency Medical Services in
the State
February 3, 2026
Senator Bailey, Representative Mathieson, and Distinguished Committee members of the Health Coverage and
Financial Services Committee, thank you for the opportunity to speak today. My name is Michael Senecal, and l serve as President of the Maine Ambulance Association and Senior Director for MaineHealth EMS and l
had the privilege of serving on the Blue Ribbon Commission to Study Emergency Medical Services in the
State
l am here to express my support for LD 2128, which implements key recommendations of the Blue Ribbon Commission. The Commission determined that the current EMS Board structure no longer reflects the realities of Maine's EMS system and recommended restructuring to ensure proportional representation
across all service models--including for-profit, nonprofit, hospital--based, municipal, volunteer, fire--based, and non-transporting services. LD 2128 fulfills this recommendation by modernizing the Board's
composition to better represent today's EMS landscape and by strengthening regional input into statewide decision--making. This restructuring will also allow the Board to be more nimble, responsive, and aligned with
its true statutory intent as the executive oversight and system-execution body for emergency medical services in Maine--ensuring governance that is more balanced, efficient, and reflective of the needs identified throughout the Commission's work
Thank you for your consideration. I am happy to answer any questions.
Michael Senecal
President
Maine Ambulance Association

Testimony of William O'Neal
Director, Maine Bureau of Emergency Medical Services (Maine EMS)
Department of Public Safety
IN SUPPORT of LD 2128
"An Act to Reorganize the Emergency Medical Services' Board to Implement the Recommendations of the Blue-Ribbon Commission to Study Emergency Medical Services in the
State"
Presented by Senator BAILEY of York
BEFORE THE JOINT STANDING COMMITTEE ON HEATH COVERAGE, INSURANCE AND FINANCIAL
SERVICES
Senator Bailey, Representative Mathieson, and honorable members of the Joint Standing Committee On Health Coverage, Insurance and Financial Services
My name is Wil O'Neal, I am the Director of Maine Emergency Medcical Services, I am here
today in strong support of LD 2128, a department bill.
This legislation represents the next critical step forward in implementing the Maine EMS Boards'
2035 Vision and 2 -year Strategic Plan and operationalizes the thoughtful recommendations of the previous Blue-Ribbon Commissions on Maine EMS.
By streamlining the current Maine Emergency Medical Services' Board----reducing the number of non-regional appointed members from 12 to 5-this bill creates a more agile and efficient
leadership structure. Designed to promulgate rules and shape policy, the Board can continue its core focus, while reorganization preserves essential expertise by maintaining representation for
dispatchers, municipal administration, EMS administrators, paramedics, and technicians, leaving maximum room to continue our important partnerships and representation from Maines' Fire and EMS Departments.
This move to improve the efficiency and agility of our existing Maine EMS Board has been in planning for some time, it is a component of our 2035 Vision and mapped out in our 2023-2025
2-year Strategic Plan for Maine EMS. This bill contains the second part of a two-phased approach not merely administrative; it builds support for a more responsive and future-ready
EMS system for all Maine citizens.
Furthermore, LD 2128 strengthens the vital link between our regional councils and state-level oversight. By requiring regional councils to regularly advise their board representatives on local
concerns and policies, we ensure that the diverse needs of Maine's geography are heard at the
highest level. The bill's requirement for an annual report to our Committee oflurisdiction by

January 1st creates a transparent mechanism for continuous improvement, allowing for proactive legislative adjustments to the Maine Emergency Medical Services System.
lam glad to provide support for any work sessions on this important topic, and happy to answer any questions. Thank you,
Wil O'Neal
Director, Maine EMS
